package_info.package_name: js-cookie-parser, xml-fast-decoder, btc-api-node, coingecko-prices, binance-price, binance-prices
package_info.package_versions: unknown (all published versions as of June-July 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are part of a coordinated, targeted supply chain attack attributed to North Korean threat actors. They are designed to execute malicious code upon installation or use, retrieve further payloads from remote servers, and facilitate the delivery of additional malware. The packages use obfuscation (Base64-encoded strings) to evade detection and are distributed via social engineering to maximize impact while minimizing exposure.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (or first function call after import)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or on first use, the code disables TLS certificate validation, creates a hidden directory in the user's home folder, conditionally installs a native module if on macOS, downloads a remote payload from https://npmaudit.com/api/v4/init, and writes it to disk.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code performs several actions that are highly unusual for a legitimate npm package: disables TLS security, creates hidden directories, conditionally executes system commands, downloads remote code, and writes it to disk. The use of Base64 obfuscation further indicates an attempt to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not disable TLS validation, download and execute remote code, or create hidden directories in the user's home folder without explicit user consent. Legitimate packages also do not obfuscate their code in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some developer tools or updaters may download binaries or dependencies at install-time, but they do so transparently and with user awareness.
key_indicators: Downloading remote payloads from suspicious domains
Conditional execution of system commands (npm install) via child_process

attack_chain.action: Victim is socially engineered to install or use a malicious npm package as part of a GitHub repository collaboration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of obfuscated malicious code upon package import or use

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated code disables TLS validation, creates hidden directory, and conditionally installs additional dependencies.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download of remote payload from attacker's server

attack_chain.action: Malicious code downloads a payload from https://npmaudit.com/api/v4/init and writes it to disk in the hidden directory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution or further use of downloaded payload (final stage malware)

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated (Base64-encoded) require statements and strings in npm package entry points
Creation of hidden directories (e.g., ~/.electron) during package import or install
Network requests to suspicious or non-standard domains at import-time
Writing downloaded data to disk without user interaction
file_indicators: Presence of .electron/cache in user home directory
Obfuscated JavaScript code in index.js or main entry point
References to atob() and Base64-encoded module names
network_indicators: Any network activity to domains not associated with the package's stated functionality
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for obfuscated code (e.g., Base64-encoded require statements), unexpected network requests during import or install, and the creation of hidden directories or files in user home directories. Flag packages that disable TLS validation or download and write remote payloads to disk. Correlate package names and behaviors with known indicators from targeted supply chain attacks.
